Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. L11·N1499unmasked layer
This neuron fires at the point where a sentence resumes its main clause after an intervening appositive/parenthetical or adverbial insert — i.e., the verb, preposition, or clause-linking word immediately following a comma/parenthesis/date phrase (e.g. "…Middlesex, **opened**", "(DiBiase) **of** Jamaica Plain", "reply on Friday **when** asked", "in **response** to", or the sentence-final ".\n" boundary); it is suppressed on ordinary head nouns/copulas inside simple descriptive noun phrases.

L11·N1528unmasked layer
Weak/near-zero peak firing lands on the word that completes a fixed verb–particle or prepositional collocation in consequence/action clauses ("know how to **deal** with", "without **pay**", "**dis**continue your use", "quickly apprehended", "invasion of Afghanistan **in** December"), while the neuron is strongly *suppressed* (large negative) on concrete object nouns like "imports", "certificate", "Ambassadors".

L11·N8867unmasked layer
This neuron fires at the onset of a parenthetical/appositive insertion that interrupts a phrase — opening "(" before a mid-phrase qualifier, or the comma/dash-introduced aside ("— read, useless —", "final, fatal") and interposed modifiers like "safety" in "toughened safety glass"; it is strongly suppressed by odd/awkward lexical substitutions in a phrase ("put right", "love seat", "creative activity").
